records.name: Gibraltar
records.summary:
Gibraltar legislates its own civil and criminal law as a self-governing territory on the Iberian peninsula's southern tip. Same-sex activity has been legal since 1993 with an equal age of consent since 2012; discrimination protections covering sexual orientation and gender reassignment date from 2007; civil partnerships followed in 2014, and same-sex marriage was enacted unanimously in December 2016 after a 2015 public consultation returned overwhelming support (3,490 replies from a 24,117-person electorate).

For a transgender visitor the standing gap is legal gender: no route exists to change legal gender, and there was no specific hate-crime provision denigrating a person for sexual orientation until, in July 2021, the Ministry for Justice said it would 'urgently' consider one after a wave of online homophobia during Pride month drew a rare public rebuke from the head of government. Governance of the territory is subject to regular scrutiny by the UK parliament's overseas-territories committee, which has pressed accountability standards across the portfolio.

sources.summary: UK House of Commons Foreign Affairs Committee, Seventh Report (2007-08) on Overseas Territories: governance chapter - covers good-governance expectations, corruption concerns (Turks and Caicos), and accountability issues across the territories including Gibraltar.

El País in English (15 Aug 2016): Gibraltar put a draft bill amending the Civil Marriage Act for same-sex marriage before Parliament after a December 2015 consultation that left Gibraltarians polarized; a government minister presided over an inter-ministerial committee weighing all viewpoints, with popular consultation and main parties suggesting support for the change.

Gibraltar Chronicle (22 Jul 2021): the Ministry for Justice and Equality said it would 'urgently' consider legislation to tackle 'disgusting lurking homophobia' following an incident of anti-gay abuse.

Wikiwand (Wikipedia mirror): LGBTQ rights in Gibraltar - legal since 1993, equal age of consent since 2012, adoption right by Supreme Court ruling 2013, civil partnerships since 2014, same-sex marriage since Dec 2016 (passed unanimously), discrimination protections for sexual orientation and 'gender reassignment' since 2007; transgender persons not allowed to change legal gender.

records.name: Bermuda
records.summary:
Bermuda decriminalised private adult same-sex conduct in 1994 (House of Assembly, 22-16) and in 2013 outlawed discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation. Same-sex marriages performed in 2017 were withdrawn the following year by a Domestic Partnership Act — the first jurisdiction anywhere to reverse marriage equality — and in March 2022 the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council upheld that restoration of the traditional-marriage definition, so partnerships, not marriage, are the available status for same-sex couples.

For a transgender visitor the more telling fact is the protection gap: there is no legal recognition of transgender people, and therefore no gender-identity-specific discrimination protection at all. Church influence is significant in local politics — when a prominent entertainer's gay-charity cruise sought to dock in 2007 the premier's colourful defence was needed against religious objections — and the tourism economy that the island depends on has repeatedly had to be pointed at inclusivity.

sources.summary: Bernews (Feb 2018): Bermuda's Governor gave assent to the Domestic Partnership Act 2017, replacing same-sex marriage with domestic partnerships for both same-sex and heterosexual couples - the reversal that made Bermuda the first jurisdiction to revoke marriage equality.

Social climate: Bermuda's AME and other churches protested a gay cruise (Norwegian Dawn, New York–Bermuda, July 12) as 'incompatible with the word of God and the Christian moral fibre' — organised religious hostility to visible same-sex couples.

LGBTQ Nation/AP (July 2013): Bermuda's Senate passed the Human Rights Amendment Act outlawing discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation (also banning age discrimination); same-sex marriage not then permitted.

Royal Gazette (14 May 1994): the House of Assembly voted 22–16 to decriminalise consensual sex between adult men, removing two Criminal Code sections — a debate that split the island, with religious leaders divided and the Christian Coalition staging marches against it.
